extra.message: Insecure Deserialization via pickle.loads on User-Supplied Data — Remote code execution on the server — full system compromise through crafted pickle payload. [verified: Same as [2]: patient_bundle_thaw_169 pickle.loads() on user-controlled bytes from body or GET blob.]

Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) via Jinja2 Template with user-controlled fragment — Remote code execution, arbitrary file read, and full server compromise via Jinja2 template injection [verified: Same as [1]: patient_jinja_cast_383 Jinja2 SSTI with user-controlled fragment; full RCE.]

OS command injection via ping host parameter — Remote code execution on the server via shell command injection [verified: Same as [0]: patient_shell_probe_395 concatenates host parameter into os.system() shell command.]

OS command injection via ping endpoint — An attacker with the ops token can inject arbitrary shell commands to execute on the server, achieving full remote command execution with the privileges of the Django process [verified: Same as [0]: patient_shell_probe_395 os.system() command injection via unsanitized host parameter.]

Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) via Jinja2 in internal ops endpoint — Attacker with ops token can execute arbitrary Python code via Jinja2 SSTI payloads (e.g., accessing __class__.__mro__ to reach os.popen), achieving full remote code execution. [verified: Same as [1]: patient_jinja_cast_383 concatenates user fragment into Jinja2 Template with no sandbox; full SSTI code execution.]

Jinja2 Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) — Remote code execution through Jinja2 template engine object traversal; attacker can execute arbitrary Python code, read environment variables, access database, and pivot within the network. [verified: Same as [1]: patient_jinja_cast_383 SSTI via Jinja2 Template('Result: ' + fragment).render(); full RCE.]

Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) via Jinja2 fragment concatenation — Remote code execution via Jinja2 SSTI, allowing the attacker to read server files, environment variables, and execute arbitrary Python code. [verified: Same as [1]: patient_jinja_cast_383 Jinja2 Template SSTI via fragment concatenation; full RCE.]

OS Command Injection via host parameter in ops/shell endpoint — Remote code execution on the server — attacker runs arbitrary shell commands in the context of the Django process. [verified: Same as [0]: patient_shell_probe_395 os.system() command injection with unsanitized host parameter.]

Server-side template injection via Jinja2 Template with user-controlled fragment — Remote code execution, arbitrary file read, and full server compromise. [verified: Same as [1]: patient_jinja_cast_383 Jinja2 SSTI with user fragment concatenated into Template string.]

OS command injection via ping host parameter in ops shell probe — Remote code execution on the server with the privileges of the Django process. [verified: Same as [0]: patient_shell_probe_395 concatenates GET 'host' directly into os.system() shell command.]

Insecure Deserialization via pickle.loads() in ops/bundle route — Arbitrary code execution via crafted pickle payload — the attacker controls the deserialized object graph and can execute arbitrary Python. [verified: Same as [2]: patient_bundle_thaw_169 pickle.loads() on user bytes; arbitrary code execution.]

Server-Side Template Injection via Jinja2 in ops/jinja route — Full remote code execution via Jinja2 template injection (e.g., accessing Python builtins through Jinja2 filters/globals). [verified: Same as [1]: patient_jinja_cast_383 SSTI via Jinja2 Template concatenation of user fragment; full RCE.]

OS Command Injection via ping in ops/shell route — Remote code execution on the server — arbitrary shell commands run with the web server's privileges. [verified: Same as [0]: patient_shell_probe_395 concatenates user 'host' into os.system() shell command with no sanitization; full RCE.]

Hardcoded Default Django SECRET_KEY — If deployed without setting DJANGO_SECRET_KEY, attackers can forge session cookies for any user (including admin), sign their own CSRF tokens, and decrypt any signed data, leading to complete account takeover. [verified: Same evidence as [9]: SECRET_KEY defaults to a well-known string (line 19-22) committed to source; without DJANGO_SECRET_KEY in the environment, all session signing, CSRF tokens, and password-reset tokens are forgeable by anyone who reads the repository.]

Hardcoded default Django SECRET_KEY — An attacker who knows the default key can forge session cookies to impersonate any user, including admins, or forge password reset tokens to take over arbitrary accounts. [verified: The hardcoded SECRET_KEY fallback 'dev-secret-change-me-only-for-local-use' (line 19-22) is present in the public repository; if deployed without DJANGO_SECRET_KEY, any attacker can forge signed cookies and password-reset tokens.]

Code Injection via eval() on User-Controlled Expression — Potential remote code execution through Python class introspection chains that bypass empty __builtins__. [verified: Same as [4]: patient_formula_cast_251 eval() with restricted builtins bypassable via class introspection.]

XML External Entity (XXE) injection — An attacker with the ops token can read arbitrary files from the server filesystem (e.g., .env with database credentials), perform SSRF to internal services, or cause denial of service via entity expansion (billion laughs attack) [verified: Same as [3]: patient_xml_fold_453 XXE via lxml etree parser with resolve_entities and load_dtd enabled.]

XML External Entity (XXE) injection via lxml parser with DTD and entities enabled — Arbitrary file read from server filesystem, internal network SSRF, denial of service [verified: Same as [3]: patient_xml_fold_453 XXE via lxml with resolve_entities=True and load_dtd=True.]

XXE Injection via Unsafe lxml XML Parser Configuration — Arbitrary file read from the server filesystem, internal network SSRF, or denial of service through entity expansion. [verified: Same as [3]: patient_xml_fold_453 XXE via unsafe lxml parser configuration on request.body.]

XXE Injection via lxml parser with entity resolution enabled — Arbitrary file read on the server (e.g., /etc/passwd, .env, database files), SSRF via external DTD retrieval, and potential denial of service via entity expansion (billion laughs). [verified: Same as [3]: patient_xml_fold_453 XXE injection via lxml XMLParser with entity resolution and DTD loading.]

XML External Entity Injection via permissive lxml parser on request body — Attacker can read arbitrary server files, perform server-side request forgery, or cause denial of service through entity expansion. [verified: Same as [3]: patient_xml_fold_453 XXE via lxml parser with load_dtd=True and resolve_entities=True.]

Arbitrary Code Execution via eval() in ops/formula route — Potential arbitrary Python code execution — even with builtins restricted, Python's introspection capabilities often allow bypassing eval() sandboxes. [verified: Same as [4]: patient_formula_cast_251 eval() with restricted __builtins__ but escapable via Python introspection chains.]

DEBUG=True by Default Exposes Sensitive Information — Information disclosure of source code, database queries, environment variables, and potentially SECRET_KEY through Django debug error pages. [verified: Same root cause as [5]: `env_bool('DJANGO_DEBUG', True)` with default True exposes stack traces, SECRET_KEY, and SQL queries on error pages reachable via Host-header spoofing against 'localhost' in ALLOWED_HOSTS.]

DEBUG Mode Enabled by Default — Information disclosure of SECRET_KEY, DATABASE_URL, environment variables, source code paths, and internal application state through Django's detailed error pages, enabling further attacks. [verified: DEBUG=True by default (line 23) displays detailed 500 pages with SECRET_KEY, DATABASE_URL, environment variables, and SQL queries; remote reachable because ALLOWED_HOSTS=['localhost','127.0.0.1'] can be bypassed with a spoofed Host:localhost header.]

DEBUG mode enabled by default exposing sensitive application internals — Exposure of SECRET_KEY, database credentials, source code paths, and stack traces to unauthenticated users [verified: DEBUG=True default (line 23) exposes SECRET_KEY, DATABASE_URL, source code paths, and stack traces through detailed error pages; .env.example reinforces DJANGO_DEBUG=1, and remote access is possible via Host:localhost spoofing.]

Any care-team clinician can release another clinician's draft visit summary — Incomplete or unverified medical information released to patients, undermining clinical data integrity and potentially impacting patient safety [verified: visit_summary_release checks @clinician_or_admin + can_view_patient (care-team membership) but has zero author check (vs.author != request.user); any care-team clinician can release any draft, exposing incomplete clinical notes to patients before the author intended. The control is genuinely absent on POST /medical/visit-summaries/<id>/release/.]

Any care-team clinician can edit another clinician's prescription — Unauthorized modification of prescription orders enabling horizontal privilege escalation and potentially dangerous medication changes [verified: prescription_edit checks @clinician_or_admin + can_view_patient (care-team membership) but has zero prescriber check (rx.prescriber != request.user); any care-team clinician can modify another clinician's prescription—medication name, dosage, instructions, status—via the full PrescriptionForm. The control is genuinely absent on POST /medical/prescriptions/<id>/edit/.]

Missing rate limiting on authentication endpoints — Attackers can brute-force passwords against multiple accounts without IP-based throttling, enumerate valid usernames/emails via timing or lockout states, and flood password-reset emails causing resource exhaustion and user annoyance. [verified: No global or IP-based rate limiting exists across login, register, or password-reset endpoints; the per-account lockout on login_view (5 failures/15 min) does not protect registration or password-reset and cannot prevent password spraying.]

User enumeration via locked-account response in login — An attacker can probe usernames/emails and identify which accounts exist in the system (by observing the 'Account temporarily locked' response vs generic 'Invalid credentials'), facilitating targeted credential-stuffing or social-engineering attacks against confirmed patient/staff accounts. [verified: Same enumeration vector as finding 1: candidate.is_locked() at line 65 executes before authenticate(), so an attacker probing usernames/emails sees HTTP 429 for locked accounts and HTTP 400 for unknowns — confirming account existence.]

Account enumeration via login lockout timing differential — Attacker can enumerate valid usernames/emails by submitting login attempts and observing whether they receive the 'locked' (account exists) or 'invalid credentials' (account may not exist) response. [verified: Same enumeration vector: candidate.is_locked() at accounts/views.py:65-68 runs before authenticate(), so a probe returns HTTP 429 for an existing locked account vs HTTP 400 for a non-existent one — confirming account existence.]

Missing rate limiting on user registration endpoint — Automated account creation for spam or resource exhaustion, large-scale user enumeration [verified: register_view (accounts/views.py:107-128) has no rate-limiting decorators, CAPTCHA, or per-IP throttle — only @csrf_protect and @require_http_methods; no django-ratelimit or similar package is present in the project.]

Missing rate limiting on password reset endpoint — Email bombing and harassment via unlimited password-reset email triggers [verified: password_reset_request (line 135) is unprotected by rate limiting; unlimited requests can spam password-reset emails to any known address, identical root cause as finding 2.]

CSV Formula Injection in Audit Log Export via entry.target — Remote code execution on the admin's machine when the exported CSV is opened in a spreadsheet application, enabling data exfiltration, malware deployment, or lateral movement within the clinic network. [verified: Attacker-controlled login username (accounts/views.py line 58: identifier from request.POST) flows unsanitized via log_event target → AuditEntry.target → CSV export at line 73. No CSV formula sanitization exists anywhere in the codebase. The cell value starts with '=', triggering formula execution when an admin opens the CSV in a spreadsheet.]

Unrestricted file upload in internal ops endpoint — Attacker with ops token can upload arbitrary files (executables, web shells, malware) to the server filesystem. If private_exports/incoming is served or accessible by other processes, this enables code execution or malware distribution. [verified: patient_filebox_slot_010 accepts arbitrary file uploads via request.body or request.FILES without content-type or extension validation, writing to private_exports/incoming.]

Missing Authentication on Internal Operations Endpoints — Unauthenticated access to internal operational data and identity endpoints by any anonymous user. [verified: Covers both [6] and [7]: patient_roster_fold_012 lacks _wrk_gate (medium — exposes ops memo) and patient_identity_ping_335 lacks _wrk_gate (low — echoes params).]

NoSQL injection in MongoDB query — An attacker with the ops token can inject MongoDB operators to bypass query logic, access unauthorized records, extract data via boolean-based blind injection, or potentially execute JavaScript via $where if enabled [verified: Same as [5]: patient_mongo_lane_412 passes user-controlled JSON filter directly to MongoDB find_one().]

NoSQL Injection via User-Controlled MongoDB Query Filter — Arbitrary MongoDB query execution, potential data exfiltration, JavaScript code execution on the MongoDB server via $where operator. [verified: Same as [5]: patient_mongo_lane_412 passes user JSON as MongoDB filter to find_one() without sanitization.]

NoSQL Injection via user-controlled MongoDB query filter — Unauthorized access to arbitrary MongoDB records, potential data exfiltration, and possible JavaScript code execution via $where operator if server-side JS is enabled in MongoDB. [verified: Same as [5]: patient_mongo_lane_412 passes user-controlled JSON body as MongoDB query to find_one().]

DEBUG mode enabled by default — Verbose Django error pages expose internal paths, database queries, configuration values, and code snippets to unauthenticated users, greatly aiding reconnaissance and exploitation of other vulnerabilities [verified: DEBUG=True default (line 23) yields verbose error pages with stack traces and configuration values; the generic exposure aids reconnaissance but the impact is lower than directly leaking credentials, and remote reachability requires Host-header manipulation.]

Session cookies missing Secure flag when DEBUG is True — Session hijacking via network sniffing on unencrypted connections. [verified: SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE is only set when `not DEBUG` (line 144-146); with the default DEBUG=True, the Secure attribute is absent, allowing cookie theft over HTTP, though SameSite=Lax and HttpOnly provide some protection.]

Session and CSRF cookies missing Secure flag when DEBUG=True — If the application is accessed over HTTP (default runserver), session cookies are transmitted in cleartext, allowing network-based attackers to hijack authenticated sessions including admin accounts. [verified: SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE and CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE are only set inside `if not DEBUG` (lines 144-146); with the default DEBUG=True, cookies lack the Secure flag, allowing transmission over plain HTTP, though SameSite=Lax and HttpOnly provide partial mitigation.]

Missing Secure cookie flags when DEBUG=True (the default) — Session and CSRF cookies transmitted over plain HTTP are visible to network sniffers on shared networks, enabling session hijacking. [verified: SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE and CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE are conditionally set only when DEBUG=False (lines 144-146); with the default DEBUG=True, cookies are transmittable over plain HTTP, enabling MITM theft on unencrypted connections, though SameSite=Lax limits cross-site attacks.]

Session and CSRF cookies lack Secure flag when DEBUG=True (the default) — Session cookies transmitted over unencrypted HTTP, enabling cookie theft via network sniffing [verified: Cookies lack Secure flag when DEBUG=True (lines 144-146) because the conditional `if not DEBUG` is false by default; session cookies can be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP, though SameSite=Lax and HttpOnly are unconditionally set.]

CSV Formula Injection in Visit Summaries Export — When the exported CSV is opened in Excel or similar spreadsheet applications, embedded formulas execute, potentially exfiltrating data, executing commands, or compromising the analyst's system. [verified: Same visit_summaries_export CSV writer at core/views.py:304-314 writes vs.title, vs.diagnosis_text, vs.care_instructions unsanitized. No compensating control in VisitSummaryForm, model validators, or middleware prevents formula injection characters.]

CSV formula injection in visit-summary and audit-log exports — Potential formula execution in spreadsheet applications when staff opens exported CSV files [verified: visit_summaries_export at core/views.py:304-308 writes clinician-authored diagnosis_text and care_instructions to CSV without formula sanitization. No validation on VisitSummaryForm fields prevents injection characters.]

CSV formula injection in visit summary export — A malicious clinician can craft a visit summary title or diagnosis starting with a formula (e.g., '=cmd|/C calc') that executes when an admin opens the exported CSV in a spreadsheet application, potentially leading to command execution or data exfiltration [verified: visit_summaries_export at core/views.py:304 writes vs.title, diagnosis_text, care_instructions to CSV entirely unescaped. VisitSummaryForm confirms no formula-injection validation exists.]

Front desk bypasses document visibility check in decision endpoint — Front desk users can verify, reject, or archive internal-only clinical documents they should not be able to see, violating clinical data segregation [verified: document_decide (line 180) is gated only by @staff_required — which includes front_desk — and never calls _document_visible(), while _document_visible explicitly blocks front_desk from is_internal_only clinical documents (lines 39-46); the endpoint is independently reachable via POST documents/<id>/decide/, and the only per-role check present is for clinicians (line 183), not front_desk.]

Any care-team clinician can edit another clinician's draft visit summary — A clinician on the patient's care team can tamper with draft clinical records (diagnosis text, care instructions, internal notes) authored by another clinician, compromising clinical integrity and audit attribution. [verified: The visit_summary_edit view at medical/views.py:188 authorizes via @clinician_or_admin + can_view_patient but never validates vs.author == request.user. Any care-team clinician can POST modified diagnosis_text, care_instructions, or clinician_notes to another clinician's draft, and form.save() at line 200 executes the write unconditionally.]

Patient chart exposes internal-only document metadata to patients — Patients can see filenames, categories, statuses, and upload dates of staff-internal clinical/insurance documents, potentially revealing sensitive operational information such as document names hinting at diagnoses or treatments [verified: Same missing is_internal_only filter in patient_chart view (line 76) — the template at templates/patients/chart.html renders original_filename, category, status, and uploaded_at for ALL documents including is_internal_only=True ones, with no role-based conditional in the template. The document_list view (documents/views.py:62) and _patient_dashboard (core/views.py:80) correctly filter these out, c]

Patient chart exposes internal-only documents to patients — A patient can view internal-only clinical documents that should only be visible to staff, potentially exposing sensitive clinical notes, diagnoses, and staff discussions. [verified: The patient_chart view fetches patient.documents.all() without filtering is_internal_only=False for patient-role users, unlike _patient_dashboard, document_list, and search views which all correctly apply that filter. However, actual document content is still gated by _document_visible() in the detail/download views — only metadata (filename, category, status, upload date) leaks.]

Business Logic Bypass — Front Desk Can Circumvent Appointment State Machine — A front desk user can create appointments with completion statuses directly, bypassing the normal workflow (requested → scheduled → checked_in → completed), which could be used for fraud, audit evasion, or creating backdated completed appointments without clinical verification. [verified: staff_appointment_create (line ~326) uses StaffAppointmentForm whose Meta.fields includes 'status' and calls form.save() directly without applying the APPOINTMENT_TRANSITIONS state machine or the role gates enforced in appointment_transition; a front_desk user can POST status=completed, bypassing the rule (line ~323) that only clinicians/admins may complete appointments.]

CSV formula injection in appointment schedule export via user-controlled reason field — Code execution in spreadsheet application when staff opens exported schedule CSV containing patient-crafted formula payloads [verified: schedule_export writes patient-submitted Appointment.reason to CSV without formula sanitization; the reason field from AppointmentBookingForm has no validation for =, +, -, or @ prefixes, and csv.writer emits the value raw.]

Non-provider care-team clinician can cancel another provider's appointment — Unauthorized cancellation of another provider's scheduled appointments by care-team clinicians [verified: appointment_transition (line ~329) guards cancellation only with patient-ownership check (if user.is_patient_role and appt.patient.user_id != user.pk: raise 404), but imposes no provider-match check for clinician roles; a care-team clinician who is NOT the assigned provider can cancel another provider's appointment, unlike the completed/scheduled/no_show/checked_in transitions which all require cl]

CSV Formula Injection in Schedule Export — When the exported CSV is opened in spreadsheet software, formulas embedded in appointment reason fields execute, potentially exfiltrating data or executing local commands. [verified: Same schedule_export sink writing Appointment.reason to CSV without formula-injection mitigation; the reason field originates from AppointmentBookingForm with no input validation for formula-starting characters, and the export path has no sanitization step.]

CSV formula injection in schedule export — A patient with a maliciously crafted name (e.g., '=cmd|/C calc'!A0, Smith') or a malicious appointment reason can inject spreadsheet formulas that execute when staff exports and opens the schedule CSV [verified: schedule_export (line ~513) writes both str(a.patient) (Patient.__str__ returning last_name, first_name) and (a.reason or '')[:200] to CSV with no formula-injection sanitization; both data sources are patient-controllable through PatientSelfForm/StaffPatientForm and AppointmentBookingForm respectively, none of which validate against formula-initiating characters.]

CSV formula injection via patient names in schedule export — Command execution in the context of the spreadsheet application when a staff member opens the exported CSV file [verified: schedule_export (line ~519) writes str(a.patient) — which renders Patient.__str__() returning f'{last_name}, {first_name}' — to CSV via csv.writer with no formula-injection prefix sanitization; PatientSelfForm and StaffPatientForm both expose first_name/last_name as plain CharFields with no regex or clean_* validation against leading =, +, -, or @, so an attacker-controlled patient name reaches th]

CSV Formula Injection in Schedule Export via Appointment Reason Field — Authenticated patient can inject spreadsheet formulas into the schedule CSV export; when staff downloads and opens the CSV, arbitrary commands execute on their machine (e.g., calc.exe on Windows, shell commands on macOS/Linux via DDE). [verified: schedule_export (line ~524) writes a.reason via csv.writer; the reason field originates from AppointmentBookingForm (accessible to any authenticated patient, CharField max_length=300, no formula-char validation), and the CSV writer applies no neutralization prefix before the cell value.]

User Enumeration via Registration Email Check — Attackers can enumerate valid user accounts by probing registration with known email addresses. [verified: Same vulnerability as [0]: unauthenticated register_view, no rate limiting, distinct email-exists error message in PatientSelfRegistrationForm.clean_email().]

Account enumeration via registration email-exists error — Attacker discovers which email addresses are registered in the clinic portal, enabling targeted phishing or credential-stuffing attacks. [verified: Same vulnerability as [0]: unauthenticated register_view, no rate limiting, distinct email-exists error message in PatientSelfRegistrationForm.clean_email().]

Open Redirect via user-controlled lane parameter — An attacker can craft a link that redirects users to a malicious phishing site after visiting a trusted ops endpoint, enabling credential harvesting and social engineering attacks. [verified: Same as [13]: patient_return_lane_145 redirects to unvalidated user lane parameter; token gate limits real-world phishing impact.]

Mass Assignment via Workset Payload Overwrite — Privilege escalation by overwriting role/approval fields in the workset to gain elevated access. [verified: patient_workset_rebind_193 merges user payload into workset via workset.update(payload); workset fields are just reflected in JSON response with no downstream auth decisions.]

Unauthenticated access to operations endpoint (patient_identity_ping_335) — Any unauthenticated user can interact with operational identity-queue functionality, bypassing the INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN gate and potentially triggering unexpected side effects in downstream systems [verified: Same as [7]: patient_identity_ping_335 lacks _wrk_gate; echoes handle/channel params without authentication.]

Weak PRNG used for security-sensitive token generation — Tokens generated by this ops endpoint are predictable if the PRNG state is known or recoverable, potentially allowing an attacker to forge or guess generated codes [verified: Same as [23]: patient_nonce_roll_403 uses random.choice() Mersenne Twister PRNG for code generation.]

SSRF with disabled TLS certificate verification — An attacker with the ops token who can influence network routing (e.g., DNS poisoning) can intercept and modify server-to-server HTTPS traffic, potentially injecting malicious responses or redirecting to internal services [verified: Same as [24]: patient_trust_drift_432 disables TLS verification but connects to hardcoded partner.invalid domain.]

Security headers explicitly disabled in ops frame endpoint — If combined with other vulnerabilities that allow HTML injection, the disabled XSS filter and permissive CSP would remove browser-side protections, making XSS exploitation easier [verified: Same as [39]: patient_frame_slip_422 sets X-XSS-Protection:0 and CSP:'' on JSON-only ops response; no practical exploitation.]

Sensitive environment variable exposed in ops trace endpoint — An attacker with the ops token gains knowledge of the Django settings module path (revealing the Python package structure) and the private exports directory location, aiding in path traversal and other targeted attacks [verified: Same as [35]: patient_trace_panel_442 exposes DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE and BASE_EXPORT_DIR; low-sensitivity configuration info.]

Weak PRNG Used for Token Generation — Attackers who observe enough token outputs can predict future nonces/codes generated by this endpoint, potentially bypassing any authentication gating that relies on these tokens. [verified: Same as [23]: patient_nonce_roll_403 uses Mersenne Twister random.choice() for token generation instead of secrets module.]

Security Headers Intentionally Disabled — Reduced browser-side protection against XSS and content injection attacks on the ops endpoint responses. [verified: patient_frame_slip_422 sets X-XSS-Protection:0 and CSP:'' on its own JSON response only; no practical impact since the endpoint returns JSON behind token gate.]

Open Redirect in ops/lane route — Phishing and social engineering — an attacker can craft a link that redirects the victim to a malicious external site after hitting the ops endpoint. [verified: Same as [13]: patient_return_lane_145 open redirect via user-controlled lane parameter; gated by token limiting exploitability.]

Sensitive Data Exposure — Environment Info Leak via patient_trace_panel_442 — Information disclosure of filesystem paths and Django configuration, aiding reconnaissance for further attacks. [verified: patient_trace_panel_442 exposes os.environ.get('DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE') and BASE_EXPORT_DIR in JSON response; low-sensitivity configuration details.]

SSRF with disabled TLS certificate verification — Man-in-the-middle attacks on the outbound HTTPS connection, potentially exposing sensitive data transmitted to the partner endpoint or allowing injection of malicious responses. [verified: Same as [24]: patient_trust_drift_432 uses ssl._create_unverified_context() but target is hardcoded partner.invalid which will not resolve.]

Sensitive information exposure in ops trace endpoint — Information disclosure of internal server paths and configuration details that assist attackers in reconnaissance and targeted exploitation of other vulnerabilities like path traversal. [verified: Same as [35]: patient_trace_panel_442 exposes DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE and BASE_EXPORT_DIR; low-sensitivity info.]

Weak Pseudorandom Number Generator in ops/nonce route — Tokens generated by this endpoint are predictable, which could compromise any system that relies on them for security decisions. [verified: patient_nonce_roll_403 uses random.choice() (Mersenne Twister) for code generation instead of secrets module; predictable tokens but endpoint is gated and codes are not used for auth.]

Disabled TLS Certificate Verification in ops/trust route — Man-in-the-middle attacks against the HTTPS connection to partner.invalid would succeed undetected, allowing interception or modification of the request/response. [verified: patient_trust_drift_432 uses ssl._create_unverified_context() disabling TLS verification; target is hardcoded partner.invalid with no real operational impact.]

Missing Secure Cookie Flags in ops/crumb route — The cookie can be read by client-side JavaScript (missing HttpOnly) and transmitted over unencrypted HTTP (missing Secure flag), enabling session/cookie theft via XSS or network sniffing. [verified: patient_crumb_lane_289 sets cookie via response.set_cookie('portal_crumb', marker) with no HttpOnly, Secure, or SameSite flags; ops endpoint behind token gate limits exploitability.]
